audit.whatIsWrong: Chart calls First item even and hands 2+ items to Gwen, but the spike text and whys[6] both say 2+ items is K'Sante's window and first item is 'your peak'.
audit.why: All Out is what flips this lane, and it needs items to matter. Gwen owns 1 through first item; K'Sante owns 2+.
audit.corrected: First item to Gwen, 2+ items to K'Sante in both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Path Maker is named as the thing to trade around six times with no cooldown given, and All Out has no cooldown either.
audit.why: Path Maker is 14/13/12/11/10s and All Out 120/100/80s. 'Poke while Path Maker is down' is a 14-second window at rank 1 — that is what makes the advice actionable.
audit.corrected: Numbers added to whys[2], the level-3 spike, Key Ability Interactions and the cooldown breakdown.

audit.whatIsWrong: The text repeatedly calls his engage a 'Q third-hit knock-up'. Ntofo Strikes is a flat 3.5s line strike that grants a stack on hit and fires a pull-in shockwave at TWO stacks — and it pulls, it does not knock up. Nothing states that Path Maker stops stunning while he is All Out.
audit.why: Two stacks, not three, changes when you have to back off, and it is a pull toward him, which is exactly how you get dragged out of Hallowed Mist. Riot's All Out text: Path Maker 'deals increased damage and no longer knocks back or stuns' — so once his ult is up his engage CC is the R knockback, not W.
audit.corrected: Stack count, pull wording and the All Out interaction stated.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every prose field is first person, and the full layer's Key Ability Interactions line calls K'Sante 'her'.
audit.why: Site voice is second person; K'Sante is male.
audit.corrected: early, mid, late and all seven whys converted; pronoun fixed.

edits.before: Track K'Sante's All Out: His duelist mode. Out-DPS it with Snip. When it is down — Snip her in your mist.
edits.after: All Out (120s at rank 1) strips his own resists and knocks you out of the mist — that is his only clean 1v1.

edits.before: - K'Sante All Out: matchup-defining — His duelist mode. Out-DPS it with Snip. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Path Maker (W): 14/13/12/11/10s — the damage-reduction charge; poke in the 14 seconds it is gone. - Ntofo Strikes (Q): a flat 3.5s, and its second stack pulls you in. - All Out (R): 120/100/80s — his only clean isolation.

edits.before: His Q pokes and Path Maker's damage reduction let him trade back, but I'm an awkward melee with no mist yet — farm with Q's tip and dodge his Q pull.
edits.after: Ntofo Strikes pokes on a flat 3.5s and Path Maker's damage reduction lets him trade back, but you have no mist yet — farm with Q's tip and dodge his pull.

edits.before: I'm still soft pre-W and he can eat any trade behind Path Maker; take CS and wait for my Q+E spike rather than fight into his knock-up.
edits.after: You are still soft pre-W and he eats any trade behind Path Maker; take CS and wait for the Q+E spike rather than fight into his pull.

edits.before: Q+E online: my %-max-HP snips plus the center true-damage snip melt his HP bar through his armor, and E resets me out before Path Maker recovers.
edits.after: Q+E online: %-max-HP snips plus the true-damage center melt his HP through his armour, and E resets you out inside Path Maker's 14s.

edits.before: I out-trade him here — every point of HP/armor he stacks just feeds my percent-HP Q while Thousand Cuts heals off his big body.
edits.after: You out-trade him here — every point of HP and armour he stacks feeds your percent-HP Q while Thousand Cuts heals off his big body.

edits.before: At 6 I mist his Q knock-up or Path Maker charge to go untargetable, then R-slow and snip him down as he wastes his commit on fog.
edits.after: At 6 you mist his Ntofo pull or Path Maker charge to go untargetable, then R-slow and snip him as he spends his commit on fog.

edits.before: Riftmaker/Nashor's is my peak — %-HP Snip Snip ignores his stacked armor and my mist's armor/MR outlasts Path Maker's brief damage-reduction window.
edits.after: Riftmaker/Nashor's is your peak — %-HP Snip Snip! ignores his stacked armour and the mist's bonus resists outlast Path Maker's short damage-reduction window.

edits.before: At 2+ items his All Out strips his own resists and knocks me out of mist to isolate me, and his scaled fighter form out-duels my AP.
edits.after: At 2+ items All Out strips his own resists, knocks you clean out of mist, and his scaled fighter form out-duels your AP.

edits.before: Land his Q third-hit knock-up or eat your trade behind Path Maker's damage reduction, then commit once your mist is on cooldown
edits.after: Land the second Ntofo Strikes stack to pull you in, or eat your trade behind Path Maker, then commit once your mist is down

edits.before: Q+E online: chunk his big HP bar with %-max-HP Snip Snip plus the center true-damage snip (ignores his armor), then E-reset out before Path Maker is back up to peel.
edits.after: Q+E online: chunk his big HP bar with %-max-HP Snip Snip! plus the true-damage center (ignores his armour), then E-reset out inside Path Maker's 14-second cooldown.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are even-ish: I'm a clunky melee with just a cone Q and no mist yet, while his Q pokes and Path Maker's damage reduction lets him eat my trades, so I just farm with the tip of Snip Snip and dodge his Q pull. The moment I hit 3 with Q+E I start winning — my %-max-HP snips chunk his fat HP bar (the center snip is true damage that ignores his armor), and E refunds its cooldown on hit so I poke and reset out before Path Maker is back to peel. Don't walk into his Q third-hit knock-up, and don't dump my trade while he's mid-Path Maker channel.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are even-ish: you are a clunky melee with a cone Q and no mist, while Ntofo Strikes pokes on a flat 3.5s and Path Maker's damage reduction lets him eat your trades — farm with the tip of Snip Snip! and dodge the pull. At 3 with Q+E you start winning: %-max-HP snips chunk his fat HP bar, the center snip is true damage that ignores his armour, and E refunds its cooldown on hit so you poke and reset out before Path Maker's 14 seconds are back. Do not walk into the second Ntofo stack, and do not dump a trade while he is mid-Path Maker charge.

edits.before: This is my lane. From 4-6 my percent-HP Q shreds him harder the more HP/armor he stacks, and Thousand Cuts heals it all back off his big body. At 6 it flips fully: when he charges Path Maker or lands his Q knock-up to commit, I drop Hallowed Mist and go untargetable so his all-in whiffs, then R-slow and snip him down while E keeps repositioning me inside the fog. Bait his Path Maker, mist his engage, and shove for plates — he can't burst me through the mist and can't out-sustain my healing.
edits.after: This is your lane. From 4-6 your percent-HP Q shreds him harder the more HP and armour he stacks, and Thousand Cuts heals it back off his big body. At 6 it flips fully: when he charges Path Maker or lands the Ntofo pull to commit, drop Hallowed Mist and go untargetable so the all-in whiffs, then R-slow and snip him down while E repositions you inside the fog. Bait Path Maker, mist his engage, shove for plates — he cannot burst you through the mist or out-sustain your healing.

edits.before: Late game flips to him, and I have to respect it. Once K'Sante has 2+ items his R, All Out, strips his own armor/MR but turns him into a fast fighter who can knock me clean OUT of Hallowed Mist and isolate me — the one thing my mist can't save me from. My %-HP Q still hurts, but his scaled tank-duelist form out-duels me in that resist-shredded 1v1. So I close this lane in the mid game: snowball plates and kills before ~25 minutes, group with my shred for objectives, and never get caught alone in his All Out range.
edits.after: Late flips to him and you have to respect it. At 2+ items All Out strips his own armour and MR but turns him into a fast fighter who knocks you clean OUT of Hallowed Mist and isolates you — the one thing mist cannot answer. Note that while he is All Out, Path Maker no longer stuns, so his CC is the R knockback itself. Your %-HP Q still hurts, but his scaled duelist form wins that resist-shredded 1v1. Close the lane in the mid game, group with your shred, and never get caught alone inside All Out range.

notes: Whether Hallowed Mist's untargetability can be broken by All Out's initial knockback specifically (versus simply displacing you out of the zone) is not answerable from the kit files; the text's existing 'knocks you out of the mist' framing was kept because it is true either way.
